messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Functions library update and questions
parts:
Before I go ahead and create the repository for the user-defined functions library, I want to find a decent name for the repository. Any preferences from the ones below (I'm not sure about them) or other suggestions?

user-function-library
function-library
stan-function-library
stan-functions
stan-language-functions

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Functions library update and questions
parts:
Also, my current thinking and initial plan is to divide the functions into four high-level categories:

lp: Functions that include statements incrementing the log probability
dist: Functions that compute (primarily the logarithms of) PDFs, PMFs, CDFs, etc.
rng: Functions that generate (pseudo) random numbers
other: Other functions (e.g. for working with Stan's various data types)

If/when we move to using _lpdf, _lcdf, etc. it would also be natural to subdivide the "dist" directory into lpdf, lcdf, lccdf, etc.

I'm also thinking about structuring the "other" directory in some way, but I'm not sure if it should be by return type (e.g. other/matrix, other/vector) or topic (e.g. other/subsetting).

Please feel free to tell me these are bad ideas (preferably also suggesting better ones)!

messages.author: a236d3d356ca53fd
messages.subject: Re: Functions library update and questions
parts:
I would guess that if someone would contribute functions for, e.g., generalized Pareto distribution, it would be better to keep gpareto_lpdf, gpareto_cdf, gpareto_rng, etc. together for potential code sharing between those functions and for easier copying to a new model. So I would have all distribution related functions in one place.

Aki
